## What These Tools Are

ART and CleverHans predate the LLM boom — they were built for attacking classic ML models (image classifiers, spam filters, malware detectors) with **evasion, poisoning, and extraction** attacks. They're still directly relevant to AI red teaming because plenty of production AI systems still rely on these classic model types (content moderation classifiers, fraud detectors, spam filters) either standalone or as a guardrail layer in front of an LLM.

## ART (Adversarial Robustness Toolbox) — IBM

ART is the more comprehensive of the two: it supports evasion, poisoning, extraction, and inference attacks across many ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, XGBoost) and many model types (not just images — also tabular and NLP).

pip install adversarial-robustness-toolbox

# With framework-specific extras
pip install "adversarial-robustness-toolbox[pytorch]"

from art.estimators.classification import SklearnClassifier
from art.attacks.evasion import FastGradientMethod

# Wrap an existing scikit-learn classifier (e.g. a spam filter, like in the Evasion module)
art_classifier = SklearnClassifier(model=my_trained_model)

attack = FastGradientMethod(estimator=art_classifier, eps=0.2)
x_adv = attack.generate(x=x_test)

preds_before = my_trained_model.predict(x_test)
preds_after = my_trained_model.predict(x_adv)
print("Flipped:", (preds_before != preds_after).sum(), "/", len(x_test))

## Example ART Output

```
Flipped: 187 / 200

Evasion success rate: 93.5%
Mean perturbation (L2): 0.184
```

This tells you 93.5% of correctly-classified inputs were flipped to the wrong label with a small, bounded perturbation — a concrete robustness metric you can put directly in a report.

## CleverHans — CleverHans Lab

CleverHans is older and more research-oriented than ART — a lighter-weight library focused specifically on generating adversarial examples (FGSM, PGD, Carlini-Wagner, and other published attack algorithms) for benchmarking model robustness.

import torch
from cleverhans.torch.attacks.fast_gradient_method import fast_gradient_method

x_adv = fast_gradient_method(model_fn, x_test, eps=0.05, norm=float('inf'))
preds_adv = model_fn(x_adv).argmax(dim=1)
print("Accuracy under attack:", (preds_adv == y_test).float().mean().item())

ART and CleverHans overlap heavily in the algorithms they implement (FGSM, PGD, etc.). Use ART when you need broad framework/model-type support and production-style workflows; use CleverHans when you specifically need a lean, research-paper-accurate reference implementation of a named attack algorithm.

## When to Reach for These

Use ART or CleverHans whenever the AI system under test includes a **classic classifier component** — a moderation filter, an anomaly detector, a fraud model — not just a chat-style LLM. This directly connects back to the white-box and black-box evasion techniques you practiced in the AI Evasion module, just with a mature library instead of hand-rolled attack code.
